revision:
1. Hierarchy & Legibility: Increase the opacity (to ~90%) and font-weight of the artist name 'ELARA VANCE' to ensure immediate identification without overpowering the title. Simultaneously, increase the font size and contrast of the 'OPEN DAILY' hours text in the footer to ensure logistical details are legible at a glance.
2. Focal Distinctiveness: Introduce a subtle, atmospheric radial gradient (deep charcoal or dusty violet) behind the geometric artwork SVG to differentiate it from the background void, creating a visual anchor that conveys 'presence' within the theme of absence.
3. Integrated CTA: Replace the stark white 'Reserve Tickets' button with a solid, textured fill (matching the artwork's gradient palette) bordered by a thin, high-contrast yellow line. This preserves the button's visual weight and prominence (Completeness) while harmonizing it with the experimental aesthetic (Unity/Variety), avoiding both the 'generic UI' look of the white block and the 'invisible' risk of a ghost button.
protected_strengths: The immersive, dark atmospheric aesthetic and generous negative space.
The strong typographic hierarchy of the main exhibition title 'ECHOES OF THE UNSEEN'.
The clean, grid-based alignment separating text (left) from artwork (right).
resolved_conflicts: Button Visibility vs. Aesthetic Unity: Resolved by using a solid, palette-matched fill with a high-contrast accent border, ensuring the CTA is prominent (Completeness) without breaking the dark mood (Unity).

Artist Name Legibility vs. Ethereal Tone: Resolved by increasing opacity and weight rather than changing font family, ensuring readability (Simplicity) while maintaining the delicate, spectral character (Variety).
Artwork Visibility vs. Negative Space: Resolved by adding a subtle background glow to the artwork container, providing focal contrast (Variety) without cluttering the overall layout (Simplicity).
rationale: This brief prioritizes the non-negotiable requirement that essential information (Artist, Hours, CTA) be immediately legible (Completeness/Simplicity) while resolving the aesthetic clash of the original button through an integrative design solution that respects the exhibition's atmospheric identity (Unity/Variety). It avoids vague compromises by specifying concrete visual treatments (opacity, gradient, textured fill) that satisfy all four mandates simultaneously.
